primitives.name: Color
primitives.list: Pick, scale, contrast, harmony, convert, blend
intro: A color is never alone. Put red beside green and both grow louder; put it on cream and it rests. What you are choosing is a relationship.
Six instruments for the recurring color problems in digital work. They use OKLCH, so steps look even to the eye, and every value is one click from your clipboard.

instruments.name: Pick
instruments.does: Choose a color by light, strength and hue
instruments.pain: You need a color, not a hex code you found somewhere

instruments.name: Scale
instruments.does: Even tints and shades from one color
instruments.pain: Your grays and tints look uneven because they were made in HSL

instruments.name: Contrast
instruments.does: Check a text color against a background
instruments.pain: You are not sure the gray text passes
instruments.fix: Lower L of A by 0.02 until ratio >= 4.5, keep C and H

instruments.name: Harmony
instruments.does: Colors that sit well with one
instruments.pain: You have one brand color and need four more

instruments.name: Convert
instruments.does: Any color format into every other
instruments.pain: The design file says one thing, the code wants another
instruments.primaryValue: the format you did not paste

instruments.name: Blend
instruments.does: What two colors make together
instruments.pain: Overlays and multiplies come out muddy

primitives.name: Type
intro: Type is language given a body. Size, weight, and the space around each line decide whether a reader keeps going.
Five instruments for the type decisions made on every project, from a modular scale to the system font that stands in before your webfont loads.

instruments.name: Scale
instruments.does: A modular type ramp with line heights, as clamp() CSS
instruments.pain: Your sizes were picked one at a time and nothing lines up

instruments.name: Specimen
instruments.does: Your text in a curated shelf of faces, with pairings
instruments.pain: Google Fonts has 1,700 families and no opinion

instruments.name: Measure
instruments.does: Line length and paragraph rhythm
instruments.pain: Lines are too long on wide screens and you cannot tell by how much

instruments.name: Units
instruments.does: px, rem, em, pt and letter-spacing conversions
instruments.pain: The spec is in points and tracking, the CSS is in rem and em

instruments.name: Fallback
instruments.does: System font stacks that match your webfont metrics
instruments.pain: Text jumps when the webfont arrives

primitives.name: Grid
intro: A grid is a decision made once so that a hundred small decisions do not have to be made later.
Four instruments for dividing space: columns and gaps as real CSS, breakpoints you can test, a baseline overlay, and common page skeletons.

instruments.name: Columns
instruments.does: Columns, gap and margin with live reflow, as CSS
instruments.pain: You want a 12-column grid and the CSS to match, not a framework

instruments.name: Breakpoints
instruments.does: Define and test breakpoints
instruments.pain: Nobody remembers why 768 and 1024

instruments.name: Baseline
instruments.does: Vertical rhythm overlay
instruments.pain: Things look slightly off and you suspect the line heights

instruments.name: Layout
instruments.does: Page skeletons as grid-template-areas
instruments.pain: You rebuild the same header, sidebar, content layout every time

primitives.name: Shape
intro: Every shape is a boundary. Where the boundary bends, softens, or breaks is most of what people feel about it.
Five instruments that produce clean SVG and CSS for the simple forms you need constantly and redraw every time.

instruments.name: Form
instruments.does: Parametric shapes exported as clean SVG
instruments.pain: You need a triangle and the SVG you found has 40 lines of cruft

instruments.name: Corner
instruments.does: Radius, squircle and smooth corners
instruments.pain: border-radius never looks like the iOS corner

instruments.name: Polygon
instruments.does: A clip-path builder
instruments.pain: Writing clip-path percentages by hand

instruments.name: Blob
instruments.does: Organic forms from a seed
instruments.pain: You need one soft shape that does not look like every other generator

instruments.name: Favicon
instruments.does: One mark exported at every size
instruments.pain: Favicons need six files and a manifest

primitives.name: Motion
intro: Movement is how an interface says what just happened. The right curve makes a change feel caused; the wrong one makes it feel broken.
Five instruments for feeling a curve before you commit to it, with values ready for CSS, Framer Motion and SwiftUI.

instruments.name: Ease
instruments.does: Easing curves played beside linear
instruments.pain: cubic-bezier numbers mean nothing until you see them move

instruments.name: Spring
instruments.does: Mass, stiffness and damping, felt
instruments.pain: Springs feel right in the app and wrong in your CSS

instruments.name: Duration
instruments.does: How long a movement should take
instruments.pain: Everything is 300ms because that is the default

instruments.name: Stagger
instruments.does: Choreography for lists
instruments.pain: Items appearing at once feel like a page load, not a reveal

instruments.name: Export
instruments.does: CSS, Framer Motion and SwiftUI values
instruments.pain: The same curve has to be written three ways

instruments.name: Scale
instruments.does: A spacing scale with live examples

instruments.name: Inset
instruments.does: Padding and margin applied to a card and a text column

instruments.name: Tokens
instruments.does: CSS variables or Tailwind config

instruments.name: Shadow
instruments.does: Layered box-shadow from a light angle and softness

instruments.name: Elevation
instruments.does: A consistent ladder of depths

instruments.name: Blur
instruments.does: Backdrop blur and translucency that stays legible

instruments.name: Grain
instruments.does: Film grain over any color

instruments.name: Gradient
instruments.does: Smooth gradients with dithering

instruments.name: Texture
instruments.does: Procedural textures exported as PNG or SVG filter

instruments.name: Aspect
instruments.does: Aspect ratios and the sizes they produce

instruments.name: Proportion
instruments.does: Golden, musical and root ratios applied to a frame

instruments.name: Crop
instruments.does: Safe areas for every platform

instruments.name: Tile
instruments.does: A repeat from one shape

instruments.name: Stripes
instruments.does: Stripes, dots and checks as CSS

instruments.name: Export
instruments.does: SVG pattern or PNG tile

instruments.name: Grid
instruments.does: A 24px icon grid with keylines

instruments.name: Stroke
instruments.does: Consistent stroke across sizes

instruments.name: Optical
instruments.does: Optical size adjustments

instruments.name: UUID
instruments.does: v4 and v7 identifiers

instruments.name: Range
instruments.does: A number between two others

instruments.name: Dice
instruments.does: Any dice, any count

instruments.name: Shuffle
instruments.does: A list in random order

instruments.name: Seed
instruments.does: Repeatable sequences from a shareable seed

instruments.name: Machine
instruments.does: States, events and transitions you can click through

instruments.name: Export
instruments.does: XState JSON or a plain switch
